jurisdiction.name: Ethiopia
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Ethiopia governs AI mainly through institutions: the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute, established by Council of Ministers Regulation 510/2022, and the Medemer AI University, established by Regulation 588/2026. The Personal Data Protection Proclamation 1321/2024 adds binding rules on automated decisions. A 2024 National AI Policy, the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy and an October 2026 draft AI governance framework have no official texts online, and a draft data governance proclamation is listed as before Parliament (not yet verified from the official text).
narrative.review_notes: This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering the federal laws portal, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. The websites of the AI Institute, the innovation ministry and several other ministries were unavailable and Parliament has no online bills tracker; the national AI policy, the draft AI governance framework, the draft data governance proclamation and education and health AI guidelines are tracked as leads.

instruments.english_title: Artificial Intelligence Institute Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation No. 510/2022
instruments.current_status: In force since publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (28th Year No. 32) on 23 April 2022 (Art. 16). Issued bilingually in Amharic and English; the Ministry of Justice portal title wrongly adds 'Customs Regulation' to the English title. Regulation No. 588/2026 makes the Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence accountable to the Institute.
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers regulation (issued under Proclamation No. 1263/2021) establishing the Artificial Intelligence Institute as an autonomous federal institution accountable to the Prime Minister, with objectives of AI research, development and deployment, setting enabling national AI policy and infrastructure frameworks, and building an AI startup ecosystem. Its powers include formulating, drafting and monitoring national AI policies, laws and regulatory frameworks, and supporting national security decision-making with AI. It transfers the rights and obligations of the AI Research and Development Center to the Institute and repeals Artificial Intelligence Center Regulation No. 463/2020.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Ethiopia's national AI body, which is mandated to draft national AI policy and regulation.

instruments.current_status: In force from publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (30th Year No. 35) on 24 July 2024 (Art. 70). Implementing directives of the Ethiopian Communications Authority were not located on official sites (see leads).
instruments.summary: Ethiopia's first comprehensive personal data protection law, applying to processing by automated and non-automated means and designating the Ethiopian Communications Authority as the regulatory authority. Article 31 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produces legal or similarly significant effects, plus rights to human intervention and to express their views, with exceptions for contracts, laws with safeguards and explicit consent; automated evaluation of personal aspects may not be based on sensitive data. Controllers must disclose the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and its envisaged effects.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law with explicit automated-decision and profiling rules that govern AI systems processing personal data.

instruments.current_status: In force from publication in the Federal Negarit Gazette (32nd Year No. 19) on 17 March 2026 (Art. 6). The Ministry of Justice portal lists it twice (a second Amharic-titled entry for the same regulation).
instruments.summary: Council of Ministers regulation, issued under the university autonomy Proclamation No. 1294/2023, establishing the Medemer University of Artificial Intelligence as an autonomous university with its main campus in Addis Ababa. Notwithstanding the general university regime, the University is accountable to the Artificial Intelligence Institute, and the Ministry of Education's powers over it are delegated to its board, which may issue implementing directives.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Extends the national AI institutional set-up: a public AI university placed under the Artificial Intelligence Institute.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: The federal laws portal (in English and Amharic), Parliament, the government and each ministry and sector regulator were searched at national level in a review redone on 2026-10-13. No qualifying AI-governance document was found for strategies, ethics, risk and assurance, public-sector rules, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, readiness indices, sector rules, generative AI, drafts and consultations, international agreements, or past instruments. AI material of the AI Institute, the innovation ministry, several ministries (finance, revenue, labour, agriculture, foreign affairs, defence), the standards institute and the competition authority remains to be checked, and the national AI policy, the final Digital Ethiopia 2030 text, the draft AI governance framework and the draft data governance proclamation remain leads to check later.
coverage_audit.technical_note:
Method note (original): This review was first completed on 12 October 2026 and redone in a longer pass on 13 October 2026, covering the federal laws portal, the government, each ministry and each sector regulator. The AI Institute's, the innovation ministry's and several other ministries' websites could not be read, and Parliament has no online bills tracker. The national AI policy, the draft AI governance framework, the draft data governance proclamation and education and health AI guidelines are tracked as leads.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: thin pass 2026-10-13 (second, longer deep review: up to 45 minutes, one agent, national level only, PROTOCOL §6; every existing record re-checked; each ministry and sector regulator searched one by one). Thin pass 2026-10-13: 3 existing records re-checked (curl for law pages and gazette PDFs, WebFetch for law pages); no content change. justice.gov.et searched in English and Amharic; Proclamations 1185/2020, 1284/2023, 1205/2020, 958/2016, 1426/2026, Regulation 582/2025, Proclamations 1358/2024 and 1396/2024 checked (no AI provisions). aii.et and pmo.gov.et client-side shells (PMO API lists empty); mint.gov.et, mof.gov.et, revenue, labour, agriculture, foreign affairs, defence, competition authority unreachable; Standards Institute 403. NBE, CMA, ECA, Media Authority, EFDA, ETA, INSA, PPPA: no AI documents. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Ministry of Justice federal law portal (justice.gov.et, mirrors the Federal Negarit Gazeta) searched in English and Amharic (laws and directives). The 3 existing records re-read (curl + WebFetch) and confirmed unchanged. Checked and out of scope (no AI provisions, only generic 'algorithm' in technical definitions): Hate Speech and Disinformation Proclamation 1185/2020, Digital ID Proclamation 1284/2023, Electronic Transaction Proclamation 1205/2020, Computer Crime Proclamation 958/2016, Critical Infrastructure Cybersecurity Proclamation 1426/2026, Electronic Signature Regulation 582/2025 and amendment Proclamation 1358/2024, Startup Proclamation 1396/2024 (general regulatory sandbox, not AI-specific). No AI law, deepfake offence, public-sector algorithm or AI procurement rule. Regulation 463/2020 (repealed AI Center) still not on the portal. Parliament: hopr.gov.et has no bills tracker or order papers online; draft National Data Governance Proclamation (forwarded 28 Sep 2026) held as a lead.; Government: Ethiopian AI Institute (aii.et): client-side shell, no content served to curl or WebFetch. Office of the Prime Minister (pmo.gov.et): app shell; its public API returns no news/publications; Digital Ethiopia 2030 PDF path still serves the app shell (lead kept). Ministry of Innovation and Technology (mint.gov.et): unreachable. National AI Policy (2024) and October 2026 draft AI governance framework: no official text (leads).; Ministries: Education (moe.gov.et resources sections checked: no AI document; Digital Education Strategy listed but not downloadable, lead; AI-in-education policy reported in drafting, lead). Health (moh.gov.et publications page and ict.moh.gov.et e-library listing: no AI document; AI TB X-ray guideline reported, lead). Justice (justice.gov.et: no AI guidance beyond the laws). Finance (mofed.gov.et: no AI mention; mof.gov.et unreachable). Revenue (mor.gov.et unreachable). Labour and Skills (mols.gov.et unreachable). Agriculture (moa.gov.et unreachable). Foreign Affairs (mfa.gov.et unreachable). Defence (mod.gov.et unreachable). Interior/police: no federal AI document found. Innovation and Technology: unreachable (see Government).; Regulators: National Bank of Ethiopia (search API: no AI content). Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (site search: only news of meetings with the AI Institute). Insurance: supervised by NBE (same result). Ethiopian Communications Authority, telecoms and data protection regulator (media library and search: only Proclamation 1321/2024 and telecom directives; no PDP directives or AI guidance). Ethiopian Media Authority (homepage: no AI content; no AI/deepfake guideline found by web search). Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority (search API: no AI or software-as-medical-device guidance). Education and Training Authority (eta.gov.et homepage: no AI content). Competition and Consumer Protection Authority (site unreachable). INSA, cyber security (documentation page lists cyber standards and frameworks, none on AI). Ethiopian Standards Institute (ethiostandards.org 403; esi.gov.et unreachable; no evidence of ISO/IEC 42001/23894/22989 adoption found by web search). Public Procurement and Property Authority (search API: e-GP news only, no AI procurement rules). Immigration and Citizenship Service (no AI document).. Not reached: aii.et (Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute: client-side shell); mint.gov.et (Ministry of Innovation and Technology: connection failed); pmo.gov.et document files (app shell; API empty); hopr.gov.et bills (no bills tracker online); Ministries of Finance (mof.gov.et), Revenue, Labour and Skills, Agriculture, Foreign Affairs, Defence: sites unreachable; Ethiopian Standards Institute (403/unreachable); Competition and Consumer Protection Authority (unreachable); MoH e-library (e-library.moh.gov.et unreachable). Could not verify: National AI Policy (2024): no official copy online; Digital Ethiopia 2030 final text and adoption date: pmo.gov.et serves only the app shell; Draft AI governance framework (Oct 2026): issuing body and text unknown, news only; Draft National Data Governance Proclamation: no official bill text; Regulation 463/2020 gazette text; Ethiopian Standards Institute AI standard adoptions (site blocked). strategy, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.issuing_authority: Council of Ministers (prepared by the Artificial Intelligence Institute / Ministry of Innovation and Technology)
leads.note: Reported approved by the Council of Ministers at its 37th regular session (27 June 2024) and cited in the Digital Ethiopia 2030 strategy as 'The AI Policy (2024)'. No official full text found on aii.et (site is a client-side app with no listed documents), mint.gov.et (connection reset) or justice.gov.et; the only online copies are on non-official hosts. Promote once an official copy is published.

leads.title: Digital Ethiopia 2030
leads.issuing_authority: Federal Government of Ethiopia (Office of the Prime Minister; Ministry of Innovation and Technology)
leads.note: Official PDF at https://www.pmo.gov.et/media/other/Digital_Ethiopia_2030.pdf (curl returned only the site's app shell; WebFetch HTTP 503). A copy labelled 'Draft' is hosted by the National Bank of Ethiopia (nbe.gov.et/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Draft_Digital_Ethiopia_2030.pdf, read in full): it integrates the National AI Policy (2024), names AI among enabling technologies, and tasks the Ethiopian Artificial Intelligence Institute with leading a National AI Strategy and overseeing an AI Innovation and Ethics Framework. No publication or adoption date stated in the document; reportedly approved by the Council of Ministers in late 2025. Record once the PMO/MInT copy and an official date are confirmed. It succeeds Digital Ethiopia 2025.
